                     </ns0:note> deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul? And the LORD said, They will deliver thee up <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">To wit, if thou abidest there. For God saw their hearts, their purposes, and passions, their aversion from <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and their affections to <ns0:hi>Saul,</ns0:hi> and knew better than themselves what they would do in that case.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 ¶ Then David and his men, <ns0:hi>which were</ns0:hi> about six hundred <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Two hundred being added to his former number, <ns0:hi>chap:</ns0:hi> 22. 2. upon his last and great Success against the <ns0:hi>Philistines.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, arose, and departed out of Keilah, and went whithersoever they could go <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Hither or thither, where they could find refuge, or an hid<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing place.</ns0:note>: and it was told Saul that David was escaped from Keilah, and he forbare to go forth.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 And David abode in the wilderness in strong holds, and remained in a mountain in the wilder<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness of Ziph: and Saul sought him every day, but God delivered him not into his hand <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">As <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> fondly persuaded himself, he intended, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 7.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 And David saw <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Either by information from his spies: or, by prospect from the top of the Mountain where he was.</ns0:note> that Saul was come out to
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:239" />
seek his life: and David <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> in the wilderness of Ziph in a wood.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 ¶ And Jonathan, Sauls son arose, and went to David in the wood <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Where <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> had appointed to meet him at that time.</ns0:note>, and strengthened his hand in God <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">He comforted and supported him against all his fears, by minding him of Gods infallible Promises made to him, and his singular Providence which hitherto had and still would be with him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 And he said unto him, Fear not, for the hand of Saul my father shall not find thee, and thou shalt be king over Israel, and I shall be next unto thee <ns0:note n="‖" place="bottom">Which he gathered either from <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s Generosity, In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />genuity, and true Friendship to him; or from some promise made to him by <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> concerning it. Or, the meaning of the words <ns0:hi>next unto thee,</ns0:hi> may be as much as to say, I shall be under thee, after thee, or inferior to thee, as the Phrase <ns0:hi>tibi secundus</ns0:hi> oft signifies. So that the whole imports thus much; I do not look to be King my self (as by my Birth I might expect), but that thou shalt be King (God having so appointed) and I but in a Secondary place inferior to thee.</ns0:note>: and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 24. 20.</ns0:note> that also Saul my father know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">By strong and well-grounded conjectures, as hath been noted.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 And they two made a covenant <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Renewed their former Covenant.</ns0:note> before the LORD <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Setting themselves as in Gods presence, and calling upon him to be Witness between them.</ns0:note>: and David abode in the wood, and Jonathan went to his house.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 ¶ Then came up the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 54. title.</ns0:note> Ziphites <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Who were of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s own Tribe, though for this their unnatural and strange carriage to him, he calls them <ns0:hi>strangers, Psal.</ns0:hi> 54. 3.</ns0:note> to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself with us in strong holds in the woods, in the hill of Hachilah, which <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> on the right hand.</ns0:note> on the south of <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> the wil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derness.</ns0:note> Jeshi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 Now therefore, O king, come down accord<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to all the desire of thy soul to come down, and our part <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">It shall be our care and business to the utmost of our power. Or, we will undertake to deliver him, or betray him to thee.</ns0:note> to deliver him into the kings hand.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 And Saul said, Blessed <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> ye of the LORD, for ye have compassion on me <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Whilst others harden their hearts against me, and joyn with <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> in his treasonable conspiracy, you shew your pity to me by your readiness to help me.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22 Go, I pray you, prepare yet <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">To wit, the matter, inform your selves certainly of things, and dispose them so that we may not be frustrated in our attempt.</ns0:note>, and know, and see his place where his <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> foot shall be.</ns0:note> haunt is <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">In what Cave, or Wood, or Mountain he is most frequently.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> who hath seen him there: for it is told me that he dealeth very subtilly.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="23">23 See therefore, and take knowledge of all the lurking places where he hideth himself, and come ye again to me with the certainty, and I will go with you: and it shall come to pass, if he be in the land, that I will search him out throughout all the thousands of Judah <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Through all the parts of that Tribe. Every Tribe was divided into Thousands, as Countries are now with us in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to Hundreds. See <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 6. 15. Or, <ns0:hi>with all the Thousands of</ns0:hi> Judah, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> I will raise against him all the Forces of that Tribe in which he trusteth and hideth himself. This he saith to animate them to the more vigorous Prosecution of him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="24">24 And they arose, and went to Ziph before Saul <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">To prepare things for <ns0:hi>Saul,</ns0:hi> who Marched after them.</ns0:note>: but David and his men <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> in the wil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derness of Maon <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Whither he went from the Wilderness of <ns0:hi>Ziph,</ns0:hi> upon suspicion or information that <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> was coming thither.</ns0:note>, in the plain on the south of Jeshimon.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="25">25 Saul also and his men went to seek <ns0:hi>him,</ns0:hi> and they told David: wherefore he came down into a rock <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Into a Cave which was in the Rock; or, which might be called a Rock, not for the height, but the strength of its situation: where at first he might think to hide himself, but upon further intelligence or consideration he removed from thence upon <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi>'s approach. Or, <ns0:hi>he came down</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>the Rock,</ns0:hi> i. e. Either, First, From the Mountain mentioned in the next Verse, whence he came down, that so he might get out of <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi>'s sight and reach. Or, Secondly, From the Hill of <ns0:hi>Hachilah,</ns0:hi> where <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> hid himself, which is said to be <ns0:hi>on the South of</ns0:hi> Jeshimon, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 19. as this place where he now was, is also described, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 24. onely that speaks of the Plain, and this of the Rock or Hill adjoyning to it, or in the midst of it. Or, <ns0:hi>he came down to</ns0:hi> Selah, as the <ns0:hi>Syriack</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Arabick</ns0:hi> translate it; a place so called from the many Rocks or Stones which were in it, or near it.</ns0:note>, and abode in the wilderness of Maon: and when Saul heard <ns0:hi>that,</ns0:hi> he pursued after David in the wilderness of Maon.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="26">26 And Saul went on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the moun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain: and David made haste to get away for fear of Saul: for Saul and his men compassed David and his men round about <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Dividing themselves into several Parties, each Marching a several way after him.</ns0:note> to take them.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="27">27 ¶ But there came a messenger unto Saul, saying, Haste thee, and come: for the Philistines have <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> spread themselves upon, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> invaded the land <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">God stirring them up by his all-disposing Providence to do it at this time for <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s rescue. Compare 2 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 19. 9.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="28">28 Wherefore Saul returned from pursuing af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter David, and went against the Philistines: there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore they called that place <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, the rock of divi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sions.</ns0:note> Sela-hammahle<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />koth <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">i. e. <ns0:hi>The Rock of divisions,</ns0:hi> because there <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> was sepa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rated, and in a manner pulled asunder from <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> who was now almost within his reach.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="29">29 ¶ And David went up from thence, and dwelt in strong holds at En-gedi.</ns0:p>
